regime_context: The detector shows a narrowly-led Hong Kong tape: only 4 of 17 themes are absolute-trend eligible (breadth_of_rotation 0.24, 'narrow'), with Banks as the lone strong leader (score 1.313 vs challenger Energy 0.983, margin 0.33). One-narrative dominance is false, crowding is benign across the board, and the validated edge is the absolute-trend gate (gate_helps true) — i.e., this is a de-risk/size-down regime read, not an alpha call. Most themes are NOT scorable (no ETF proxy), so this note runs lean on gradable theses.
emerging_watch: Energy (H-shares) is the challenger (score 0.983, durability_bar 0.76, hurst 'trend', breadth 0.8 — actually the strongest breadth in the book). Watch for a CONFIRMED leader handoff: if Energy's score overtakes Banks AND Banks' durability_bar falls below 0.5 on two consecutive observations, that would retire this watch and flag Energy as the new leader. Until then it is a watch, not a call.

theses.subject: China Tech & Internet
theses.thesis: This is the one scorable negative-momentum theme (score -0.792, rank 13/17). It sits BELOW the absolute-trend gate (eligible false) with a mean-revert Hurst tag, which — given gate_helps is true — is the one validated de-risk signal: staying exposed to gate-ineligible themes has historically meant shallower drawdowns when avoided. I would avoid/lower weight here, not short.
theses.dissent: Mean-revert Hurst tags can snap back hard on a single policy headline (e.g., platform regulation relief), and the gate avoids drawdowns but gives up the reflex bounce — avoiding an oversold, mean-reverting theme can miss a sharp V-reversal.

falsifier.text: 3033.HK closes above its 20-day moving average and holds for 5 consecutive sessions before the check-by date

theses.subject: China Platform Megacaps
theses.thesis: The worst-ranked theme (score -1.075, rank 15/17), gate-ineligible with mean-revert Hurst. Same discipline read as China Tech & Internet — this is the weakest absolute-trend regime in the book, and avoiding gate-ineligible themes is the validated risk-control leg. Both tech themes share the 3033.HK proxy, so this is a single-trade view expressed twice; I mark it low conviction to avoid double-counting.
evidence: same etf_proxy: 3033.HK as China Tech & Internet
theses.dissent: Platform megacaps are policy-sensitive and prone to gap moves on regulation headlines; a single easing signal could reverse the entire status quo. Avoiding them as a pair with China Tech & Internet means the two theses are not independent.

falsifier.text: 3033.HK posts two consecutive weekly closes above its prior 4-week high before the check-by date

theses.subject: Banks (H + HK)
theses.thesis: The sole durable leader: highest score (1.313), highest durability_bar (0.67), eligible, broadest among the leaders (breadth 0.692), and the rotation leader with no one-narrative crowding. This is a trend-following, vol-aware continuation lean — the absolute-trend gate says stay with what is working and showing breadth, NOT a return forecast. Crowding_z 0.93 is a size-down caution only, and I am not fading it.
theses.dissent: Banks are the textbook reflexivity trap — leadership with rising attention often marks a local top, and breadth 0.692 is decent but not dominant. A policy or rate shock that hits H-share bank margins would unwind this fast, and the crowding_z 0.93 is closer to the caution zone than it looks.

falsifier.text: Banks (H + HK) relative to Hang Seng turns negative over a rolling 10-day window before the check-by date

check.reason: theme has no scalar etf_proxy → not cleanly scorable

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
